Malware Analysis and Classification from Behavioral API Multigraphs Using Advanced Learning Techniques

Abstract:

Malware is a major threat to modern software systems, making effective malware analysis and family classification an important cybersecurity task. Dynamic analysis provides useful information about malware behavior, particularly API calls andtheir execution patterns. However, conventional representations may not fully capture the relationships among these behavioral activities. In this work, we represent malware behavior using behavioral API multigraphs, where API interactions during execution are modeled as connected behavioral structures. We develop a graph neural network (GNN)- based framework to learn these behavioral patterns and classify malware into different
families. We evaluate the developed framework using dynamic malware reports from the AvastCTU Public CAPEv2 dataset and compare it with different baseline and graph-based models. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of behavioral graph representation for malware family classification. Furthermore, the work will be extended by incorporating LLM-based semantic information and multimodal learning to develop an advanced intelligent framework for malware family analysis and identification. The objective is to improve the representation, analysis, and classification of malware behavior using advanced learning techniques.
